dedupe_keys.name: janus land use and land cover change model

description: Janus is an agent-based land-change model from Boise State University LEAF and collaborators. Individual agents retain or change crops according to expected profits and their tendency to switch. The Python package prepares land-cover inputs, accepts GCAM-USA or synthetic price signals, and writes NumPy arrays of land cover, agent state and profit over time. Its examples use US county boundaries and Cropland Data Layer inputs, with documented one- and three-kilometre grid options. Users define the simulation horizon and domain. The model can inform agricultural land, food-supply and irrigation-demand scenarios. Code is free under its licence labelled BSD 2-Clause, with a separate naming restriction in the text. Janus complements broader land and energy-water models through local decision representation. A limitation is the need to adapt category crosswalks, input paths and behavioural parameters; some preprocessing uses a USDA NASS API key. No key was requested, and no data supplement, model run or behavioural calibration was performed.
inputs: Initial land cover, county boundaries and crop-category crosswalk
Crop profit signals and agent switching parameters
